Closed subsets of a complete TVS are complete; however, if a TVS <math>X</math> is not complete then <math>X</math> is a closed subset of <math>X</math> that is not complete. 
The empty set is complete subset of every TVS. 
If <math>C</math> is a complete subset of a TVS (the TVS is not necessarily Hausdorff or complete) then any subset of <math>C</math> that is closed in <math>C</math> is complete.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=115-154}}

'''Topological complements'''

If <math>X</math> is a non-normable [[Fréchet space]] on which there exists a continuous norm then <math>X</math> contains a closed vector subspace that has no [[topological complement]].{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=190-202}} 
If <math>X</math> is a complete TVS and <math>M</math> is a closed vector subspace of <math>X</math> such that <math>X / M</math> is not complete, then <math>H</math> does {{em|not}} have a [[topological complement]] in <math>X.</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=190-202}}

'''Subsets of completions'''

Let <math>M</math> be a [[Separable space|separable]] locally convex [[metrizable topological vector space]] and let <math>C</math> be its completion. If <math>S</math> is a bounded subset of <math>C</math> then there exists a bounded subset <math>R</math> of <math>X</math> such that <math>S \subseteq \operatorname{cl}_C R.</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=190-202}}

'''Relation to compact subsets'''

A subset of a TVS ({{em|not}} assumed to be Hausdorff or complete) is [[Compact space|compact]] if and only if it is complete and [[totally bounded]].{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=55-56}}<ref group=proof>Suppose <math>S</math> is compact in <math>X</math> and let <math>\mathcal{C}</math> be a Cauchy filter on <math>S.</math> Let <math>\mathcal{D} = \left\{\operatorname{cl}_S C ~:~ C \in \mathcal{C}\right\}</math> so that <math>\mathcal{D}</math> is a Cauchy filter of closed sets. Since <math>\mathcal{D}</math> has the finite intersection property, there exists some <math>s \in S</math> such that <math>s \operatorname{cl}_S C</math> for all <math>C \in \mathcal{C}</math> so {<math>s \in \operatorname{cl} \mathcal{C}</math> (that is, <math>s</math> is an accumulation point of <math>\mathcal{C}</math>). Since <math>\mathcal{C}</math> is Cauchy, <math>\mathcal{C} \to x</math> in <math>S.</math> Thus <math>S</math> is complete. That <math>S</math> is also totally bounded follows immediately from the compactness of <math>S.</math></ref> 
Thus a closed and [[totally bounded]] subset of a complete TVS is compact.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=55-66}}{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=47-66}}

In a Hausdorff locally convex TVS, the convex hull of a [[Totally bounded space#Topological vector spaces|precompact]] set is again precompact.{{sfn|Trèves|2006|p=67}} Consequently, in a complete locally convex Hausdorff TVS, the closed convex hull of a compact subset is again compact.{{sfn|Trèves|2006|p=145}}

The convex hull of compact subset of a [[Hilbert space]] is {{em|not}} necessarily closed and so also {{em|not}} necessarily compact. For example, let <math>H</math> be the separable Hilbert space [[Lp space|<math>\ell^2(\N)</math>]] of square-summable sequences with the usual norm <math>\|\cdot\|_2</math> and let <math>e_n = (0, \ldots, 0, 1, 0, \ldots)</math> be the standard [[orthonormal basis]] (that is <math>1</math> at the <math>n^{\text{th}}</math>-coordinate). The closed set <math>S = \{0\} \cup \left\{\tfrac{1}{n} e_n\right\}</math> is compact but its convex hull <math>\operatorname{co} S</math> is {{em|not}} a closed set because <math>h := \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \tfrac{1}{2^n} \tfrac{1}{n} e_n</math> belongs to the closure of <math>\operatorname{co} S</math> in <math>H</math> but <math>h \not\in\operatorname{co} S</math> (since every sequence <math>z \in \operatorname{co} S</math> is a finite [[convex combination]] of elements of <math>S</math> and so is necessarily <math>0</math> in all but finitely many coordinates, which is not true of <math>h</math>).{{sfn|Aliprantis|Border|2006|p=185}} However, like in all complete Hausdorff locally convex spaces, the {{em|closed}} convex hull <math>K := \overline{\operatorname{co}} S</math> of this compact subset is compact.{{sfn|Trèves|2006|p=145}} The vector subspace <math>X := \operatorname{span} S</math> is a [[pre-Hilbert space]] when endowed with the substructure that the Hilbert space <math>H</math> induces on it but <math>X</math> is not complete and <math>h \not\in K \cap X</math> (since <math>h \not\in X</math>). The closed convex hull of <math>S</math> in <math>X</math> (here, "closed" means with respect to <math>X,</math> and not to <math>H</math> as before) is equal to <math>K \cap X,</math> which is not compact (because it is not a complete subset). This shows that in a Hausdorff locally convex space that is not complete, the closed convex hull of compact subset might {{em|fail}} to be compact (although it will be [[Totally bounded space|precompact/totally bounded]]).

Every complete totally bounded set is relatively compact.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=47-66}} 
If <math>X</math> is any TVS then the quotient map <math>q : X \to X / \operatorname{cl}_X \{0\}</math> is a [[Open and closed maps|closed map]]{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=107-112}} and thus <math>S + \operatorname{cl}_X \{0\} \subseteq \operatorname{cl}_X S</math> A subset <math>S</math> of a TVS <math>X</math> is totally bounded if and only if its image under the canonical quotient map <math>q : X \to X / \operatorname{cl}_X \{0\}</math> is totally bounded.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=12-35}} Thus <math>S</math> is totally bounded if and only if <math>S + \operatorname{cl}_X \{0\}</math> is totally bounded. In any TVS, the closure of a totally bounded subset is again totally bounded.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=47-66}} 
In a locally convex space, the convex hull and the [[Absolutely convex set|disked hull]] of a totally bounded set is totally bounded.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=67-113}} If <math>S</math> is a subset of a TVS <math>X</math> such that every sequence in <math>S</math> has a cluster point in <math>S</math> then <math>S</math> is totally bounded.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=12-35}} A subset <math>S</math> of a Hausdorff TVS <math>X</math> is totally bounded if and only if every ultrafilter on <math>S</math> is Cauchy, which happens if and only if it is pre-compact (that is, its closure in the completion of <math>X</math> is compact).{{sfn|Horváth|1966|pp=145-149}}

If <math>S \subseteq X</math> is compact, then <math>\operatorname{cl}_X S = S + \operatorname{cl}_X \{0\}</math> and this set is compact. Thus the closure of a compact set is compact<ref group=note>In general topology, the closure of a compact subset of a non-Hausdorff space may fail to be compact (for example, the [[particular point topology]] on an infinite set). This result shows that this does not happen in non-Hausdorff TVSs. The proof uses the fact that <math>S</math> is compact (but possibly not closed) and <math>\operatorname{cl}_X \{0\}</math> is both closed and compact so that <math>S + \operatorname{cl}_X \{0\},</math> which is the image of the compact set <math>S + \operatorname{cl}_X \{0\}</math> under the continuous addition map <math>\cdot + \cdot : X \times X \to X,</math> is also compact. Recall also that the sum of a compact set (that is, <math>S</math>) and a closed set is closed so <math>S + \operatorname{cl}_X \{0\}</math> is closed in <math>X.</math></ref> (that is, all compact sets are [[relatively compact]]).{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|p=156}} Thus the closure of a compact set is compact. Every relatively compact subset of a Hausdorff TVS is totally bounded.{{sfn|Horváth|1966|pp=145-149}}

In a complete locally convex space, the convex hull and the disked hull of a compact set are both compact.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=67-113}} More generally, if <math>K</math> is a compact subset of a locally convex space, then the convex hull <math>\operatorname{co} K</math> (resp. the disked hull <math>\operatorname{cobal} K</math>) is compact if and only if it is complete.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=67-113}} 
Every subset <math>S</math> of <math>\operatorname{cl}_X \{0\}</math> is compact and thus complete.<ref group=proof>Given any open cover of <math>S,</math> pick any open set <math>U</math> from that cover that contains the origin. Since <math>U</math> is a neighborhood of the origin, <math>U</math> contains <math>\operatorname{cl}_X \{0\}</math> and thus contains <math>S.</math></ref> In particular, if <math>X</math> is not Hausdorff then there exist compact complete sets that are not closed.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=47-66}}
